title: Remove the short member: what happens to the mean?
description: A family is measured again without the one far height, and the mean jumps while the median barely moves. Keeko doubts that both change by the same amount.
teaching_notes: One idea: an outlier pulls the mean much more than the median. Watch for children who expect both to change by the same amount.

source: Find the mean and median of Ruhee's family without the ou
video_script.why: The child has found the mean and median of Ruhee's family and now removes the far value.
video_script.substitution: The mean uses every value's size; the median uses only the middle position.
video_script.anchor: Ruhee's family: 170, 173, 165, 118, 175 cm; mean 160.2, median 170. Leave out 118.
video_script.wrong_answer: both change by the same amount
video_script.wrong_move: expects the mean and the median to move together when the same value is removed
video_script.payoff_line: The mean rises a lot, but the median hardly moves

final_answer.spoken: the new mean is one hundred and seventy point seven five centimetres, and the new median is one hundred and seventy one point five centimetres

names.Ruhee: family whose heights include one short member

hold_back: The mean rises a lot, but the median hardly moves
maths_rules: outlier: a value far from the rest
video_script.design: One idea: an outlier tugs the mean. The sorted row of heights stays in the anchor; the 118 figure steps out; two gauges show the mean and the median.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>The mean and the median of the family are already marked.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>What happens to each if we leave out the shortest member?

<bookmark mark='g2'/>A value far from the rest is called an outlier.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The other four are all between one hundred and sixty five and one hundred and seventy five.

<bookmark mark='g3'/>Then one hundred and eighteen, and one hundred and seventy five.
<bookmark mark='g4'/>The mean was one hundred and sixty point two, and the median was one hundred and seventy.

<bookmark mark='d2'/>The four heights add up to six hundred and eighty three.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>Divided by four, the mean is one hundred and seventy point seven five.

<bookmark mark='e3'/>The median is halfway between them, one hundred and seventy one point five.

narration: <bookmark mark='f1'/>Step four, compare with the family before.
<bookmark mark='f2'/>The mean went from one hundred and sixty point two to one hundred and seventy point seven five.
That is a change of ten point five five.
<bookmark mark='f3'/>The median went from one hundred and seventy to one hundred and seventy one point five.
That is a change of only one point five.

<bookmark mark='ans2'/>The new mean is one hundred and seventy point seven five centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's thought bubble shows two gauges, mean and median, moving by the same amount; then the mean gauge jumps far and the median gauge moves a little

marks.doubt: the bubble with two gauges moving by the same amount appears
marks.fix: the mean gauge jumps far while the median gauge moves a little
marks.idea: the middle place of the sorted row lights up, with only a small shift

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks both change by the same amount, because the same height is left out.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The mean feels the size of every height, so one far value moves it a lot.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>The median feels only the middle place, so it shifts by only a little.
